_note: M-MODES WeaponCatalog (docs/spec/modes.md §3). EVERY weapon is now based on ITS OWN captured Callsign $WEAP frame (`capture.frame`, traced to `capture.src` in protocol/captures/raw/; regenerate the decode with `python -m brx_mcp.weapmap protocol/captures/raw/*.btsnoop`; named table in docs/reference/weapons.md). That inherits every native behaviour we cannot synthesise: 3-round burst (t23), bolt/single-shot, charge, overheat (t24/t35), per-weapon reload chains, damage type (t3), reload type (t19), muzzle flash (t25/t26). `reload_type` (F123, 2026-09-11) is an EXPLICIT per-weapon attribute and is deliberately NOT read off `capture.frame` t19: t19 is unconfirmed as reloadType (the Plasma Sniper shell-reloads at t19=0 — protocol/callsign-extract/protocol-classes.md), so the only value set here is the one the wire actually proved. 'chain' = the reload is a HELD per-shell chain, `reload_ms` is the PER-SHELL interval, and a momentary button cannot drive it (the Shotgun: after $BUT,2,1 the $ALCD mag walks 1→6 at 417/423/390/420/420 ms, one reserve decrement per shell). Absent = a normal magazine reload. `wire` lists ONLY the tokens we deliberately overwrite for balance; mag/reserve/reload_ms are written too (t16/t39, t17/t40, t18) keeping the captured invariants t39==t16 and t17==2*t40. Everything else is emitted byte-for-byte as Battle Company sent it. stats: dmg/rof/rng are 0-100 UI bars derived from the real numbers. dmg = share of a 115 pool one hit removes, rof = cycle relative to the fastest weapon, rng = the wire's t41 gunRange (identical on all guns: t41 `gunRangeIndoor` was PROVEN INERT outdoors 2026-09-17, F231/Q15, and stays byte-identical to the capture -- it is deliberately never written by `resolve()`, so `rng` stays a flat 75/20 on purpose; see weapon-design.md §4.2). The venue range lever is `$WEAP` t2 `gunRangeOutdoor`, fed by `wire.range_outdoor_pct` (F234, 2026-09-17 garden test). t2 sets the emitter's CARRIER FREQUENCY, not its power (V4_31 disassembly, 2026-09-18, protocol/brx-protocol.md): a low value detunes the word out of the receiver's band-pass near 38 kHz, it does not shorten the beam, so read the shelf below as the pass-band and these values as UNCALIBRATED. It is written ONLY when the venue is 'outdoor' and the row has one -- a row with none, or any indoor/unset venue, keeps its captured t2 (100 on every gun captured so far, 90 on melee); `compile.gun_range_outdoor_pct` refuses a value under 13 (F231's measured floor: t2=5 landed 0 hits from 38 shots at any distance). `range_band` ('close'/'mid'/'full') and `range_target_m` are human-facing catalogue copy for the armoury screens, in metres, and are NEVER read by the frame builder -- they describe the same intent as `wire.range_outdoor_pct` without being the wire value, and only the SMG (30) and Shotgun/Rocket Launcher/Rail Gun (22) sit at or inside the measured 13-26 transition band, so those four are real guesses pending S49's portable receiver; everything at 55 and up is expected to behave alike until the shelf (~31-100) is mapped. 'verified' now means SHIPPED EXACTLY AS CAPTURED (no balance edit, `range_outdoor_pct` included); 'captured' is true for all 19. 'melee' is hidden (slot 4). tags: policy vocabulary (docs/spec/loadout.md §1.1). 'heavy' = role power (rocket/rail/laser cannon/energy launcher/ion sniper), 'sniper' = the four long guns incl. AMR, plus the role name; presets exclude by tag so a new weapon only needs the right tags. `class` (2026-09-17, arsenal review): 'ballistic' | 'energy' | 'melee', on every row; ballistic weapons reload, energy weapons overheat or charge. `hidden` (2026-09-17 arsenal cut): force_rifle, bolt_rifle, stinger, plasma_sniper, laser_cannon, ion_sniper, energy_launcher and glock are hidden from the picker alongside melee, cutting overlap in a 22-weapon catalogue; the row and its capture frame stay (custom games, and the pistols' based_on copy of bolt_rifle's frame, still use them). `pickup_only` (2026-09-17): rocket_launcher, rail_gun, laser_cannon, ion_sniper and energy_launcher (the 'heavy' tag) are never in a player's starting loadout pool, whatever the preset; they stay in the catalogue for a future pickup/station mechanism (docs/spec/loadout.md). `rounds_per_charge` (2026-09-17, F226/S43 bench): on the Charge Rifle only, one full charge costs this many rounds of the `mag`/`reserve` cell (10, bench-measured); every place that turns `mag`/`reserve` into a hits-or-kills count for this weapon must divide by it first (`mag // rounds_per_charge` full charges), never read the raw round count as a hit count. Absent = 1 (every other weapon fires one round per hit). recoil (S42, 2026-09-17): a TARGET accuracy profile {ceiling, floor, per_shot, recover_ms} -- declared here, wired nowhere in resolve() (t21==t22==100 stays the shipped baseline, native walk off, F230); app/src/engine.js is the only thing that drives it, pinning both wire tokens to the live value on every write so nothing depends on the native walk. A weapon with no real recoil (the power tier, the bolt guns, the shotgun, melee) ships ceiling==floor and per_shot 0. `lethal` (2026-09-18, §7.4): set FALSE on a weapon that deliberately cannot kill, which today means the fn-20 stripper (it removes every protective layer, carries overflow between them and never touches health) and the fn-23 smoke (the target's accuracy falls to 0 for about three seconds). The flag is how a row says the zero damage is a DESIGN, not the Energy Launcher accident: `validate()`'s three unkillable-weapon errors skip a row that carries it, and in exchange it enforces the placement rule, that a support weapon may never be a PRIMARY. Carrying one costs the player their backup gun, and that cost is what makes it fair. Absent = an ordinary lethal weapon. `ap_dmg` + `ap_fire_ms` (2026-09-18, weapon-design.md §7.7): what this weapon becomes while the Armour Piercing perk is on it. BOTH levers are needed and that is the whole finding. Bypassing armour takes a standard target from a 115 pool to 45 HP, and 45/115 is 0.39, so the shipped 0.4 multiplier left hits-to-kill UNCHANGED and the perk free: it was strictly better on 11 of 13 weapons. Damage alone cannot fix it either, because damage is an integer and the steps are too coarse (on an 8-damage weapon, 3 is free and 2 is useless, with nothing between). Dropping the CYCLE as well makes the trade continuous, so every plain-damage weapon can carry the perk: heavier rounds, fewer of them, slower. The pair is chosen to land the time to kill in the MIDDLE of the window between plain-against-bare and plain-against-armoured, so the cost is felt rather than technical, and `ap_fire_ms` is never faster than the weapon's own cycle. A weapon with no pair cannot carry the perk and `_refuse_if_ap_ineligible` says so. caution: optional human copy for a weapon with a known LIVE problem. The UIs show it on the tile and hero. based_on (2026-09-04, sidearms): a weapon with NO capture of its own names the captured weapon whose frame it is built on and why; its capture block is a COPY of that frame (same src), `captured: false`, and every deviation is a wire/override token. 'sidearm' = the three pistols (usp/glock/deagle, role sidearm, cls 10): slot-2 backups by design, deliberately dominated by primaries (test_ttk_band exempts them from BEING dominated, never from dominating). Fire sounds P16/Q04/X14 (glock/usp/deagle, ear-confirmed 2026-09-11) are ids no other weapon uses, so a custom .LTP over the data port (community-notes.md) replaces only that pistol.

weapons.name: Assault Rifle
weapons.desc: The one everything else is measured against. Nothing it does is remarkable, and there is no fight it cannot hold.
weapons.notes: The anchor, and the real stock M4 cadence. 13 hits at 100ms with 32 up and 192 in reserve: 17 kills without resupply and a 1.20s kill. 2026-09-17 arsenal review: cycle is back to Battle Company's native 100ms (it was throttled to 140ms so a deep reserve could not also out-cycle the field); the dominance test now grades on one-magazine kill chance rather than total kills, so the reserve alone no longer has to carry the whole weight of keeping the AR in check.

weapons.name: Burst Rifle
weapons.desc: Three rounds a pull, and the gun decides the gap rather than your finger. Slower to the kill than the rifle, and far harder to waste.
weapons.notes: A real three-round burst: one pull, three rounds, and the gun enforces the gap. 11 hits from a 36-round mag with 216 behind it; the most total ammo of the burst pair, and the tighter of the two. 2026-09-17 arsenal review: damage raised 9 to 11 so the burst pair separates further from the SMG-class assault weapons on hits-to-kill, not only on cadence.

weapons.name: Force Rifle
weapons.desc: A heavier round on the same frame. Fewer hits to land, and you feel every one of them in the recovery.

t33.why: captured D21 plays a 'disable' chirp alongside the reload, reproduced on the bench 2026-08-26; D02 is the clean cocking beat the AR/burst/bolt chains already end on

weapons.notes: The burst rifle's heavier twin: same three-round pull, more per round. 12 hits instead of 13 and a faster kill, paid for with two-thirds the reserve and a slower five-part reload.

weapons.name: Bolt Rifle
weapons.desc: One round at a time, deliberately. It asks you to aim and pays you back in hits that count.
weapons.notes: Single shot, deliberate cadence. 13 a hit every 225ms with 18 up and 180 back. That is 22 kills from a full kit, for operators who would rather aim than hold.

weapons.name: SMG
weapons.desc: A hose. The magazine leaves faster than you meant it to, and getting it back means standing still for a long time.
weapons.notes: A hose that runs hot. 8 a hit every 95ms from a 72-round mag: four kills before you reload, 24 across the kit, and an overheat budget that punishes holding the trigger down forever.

weapons.name: Shotgun
weapons.desc: Three pulls and it is over, if you were close enough to mean it. Shell by shell, and the fastest recovery on the board.
weapons.notes: Shell by shell, and the fastest recovery on the board. One pull sends two words: 20 from the gun and 20 from the shooter's own headset, both landing at any range this game is played at, 40 together. Three hits drop a target, six in the tube and a 400ms shell reload. Sustained pressure from the shallowest ammo pool outside the power tier.

weapons.name: Stinger
weapons.desc: Heavy rounds on a slow cadence. It rewards a steady hand and punishes a panicked one.
weapons.notes: Fast, light, relentless. 15 a hit every 250ms with 18 up and 144 in reserve: eight hits to drop, twenty kills to spend, and nothing held back for range.

weapons.name: Sniper Rifle
weapons.desc: Two hits from anywhere on the field, with a long moment in between to think about the first one.

t33.why: captured D21 plays a 'disable' chirp alongside the reload, reproduced on the bench 2026-08-26; D02 is the clean cocking beat the AR/burst/bolt chains already end on

weapons.notes: Two hits, one lane, a bolt between them. 60 a hit on a 1.5s cycle with four in the mag and 24 behind it. The fewest hits to a kill outside the power tier, and no margin for a miss.

weapons.name: Plasma Sniper
weapons.desc: A marksman's weapon that refuses to wait. Closer to a rifle's cadence than a scope's.
weapons.notes: A marksman rifle that fires like a carbine and pays for it in heat. One pull sends two words, 25 from the gun and 10 from the shooter's own headset, 35 together: four to drop, ten up and 80 back. Lean on it and it overheats.

weapons.name: AMR
weapons.desc: Anti-materiel, and it reads like it. Heavy hits at a pace nothing else at that range can match.
weapons.range_target_m: full reach indoor / 60m+ outdoor (Q15, tagged sniper)

t33.why: captured D21 plays a 'disable' chirp alongside the reload, reproduced on the bench 2026-08-26; D02 is the clean cocking beat the AR/burst/bolt chains already end on

weapons.notes: Anti-materiel weight at a rifle's cadence. 24 a hit every 400ms, five hits to a kill, 14 up and only 56 behind. The hardest-hitting automatic, and the shallowest.

weapons.name: Suppressor
weapons.desc: Quiet, and no muzzle flash. The only weapon that does not tell the field where you are, bought with the slowest kill in the game.
weapons.range_target_m: 15 indoor / 30 outdoor (Q15, as the LMG-role deep-mag automatic)
weapons.notes: Quiet, not silent, and no muzzle flash. It is the only weapon here that hides where you are. 8 a hit every 140ms with 75 up and 384 in reserve: 30 kills, the deepest magazine AND the deepest sustained pool, the slowest kill. 2026-09-17: mag 48→75 -- the family-scoped dominance test (§2.3) paired it against the SMG (same fire mode, same weapon_class), which beat it on every other axis; the deeper magazine gives the Suppressor an outright lead on kills-per-clip (5 vs the SMG's 4), which is the smallest change that stops the SMG strictly dominating it.

weapons.caution: Overheats after about 30 rounds of full auto, and it does not cool on its own: work the reload lever to vent the heat (about three pulls, or one held pull), then keep holding to recharge the cell.
weapons.name: Energy Rifle
weapons.desc: The cell barely stops. When it finally does, the recharge is long enough to lose the fight you were winning.
weapons.range_target_m: 15 indoor / 30 outdoor (Q15, as the LMG-role deep-mag automatic)

t38.why: F229 bench, 2026-09-17: t38 = 150 alone switches the Energy Rifle's overheat on (captured at t38 blank, so it shipped inert). Heat climbs about +3 net per shot, locks at about 99 (roughly 30 shots), and does not fall on its own while locked -- the reload lever is hold-to-recharge, and the SAME hold that refills the cell vents the heat; there is no separate cooldown. A lockout clears only by working the lever, about three taps or one held pull

t35.why: F229 bench, 2026-09-17, ear-confirmed by Tony on a real overheat ("yeah nice"): D11 (the SMG's captured overheat sound) is right. The captured D122 "sounds like it reloaded", not overheated

weapons.notes: A 300-cell battery that barely stops. 9 a hit every 150ms, 23 kills on one magazine and 69 across the kit. The largest ammo pool in the game, on the smallest per-hit number. 2026-09-17 bench (F229): now genuinely overheats — full auto locks it out around heat 99 after about 30 shots, and unlike the Charge Rifle it does not cool on its own; only the reload lever (a hold, not a tap) vents it.

weapons.name: Charge Rifle
weapons.desc: Hold it, and it holds. A full charge and two taps ends anyone, which is why it belongs to whoever saw the other person first.
weapons.range_target_m: full reach indoor / 60m+ outdoor (Q15; it charges behind cover, then reaches)

t35.why: Bench 2026-09-18, ear-confirmed by Tony on a real lockout. The captured C19 is the sound a charge makes when you release it early, not an overheat: "sounds like a charge cancel not an overheat". Re-armed with D11, the SMG's captured overheat sound, on the same gun in the same minute: "that one sounds right, use D11". The Energy Rifle already ships the same id for the same reason (F229)

weapons.notes: Pre-charge it behind cover, then the kill is one release and two taps: an 85-damage charge (held indefinitely, 3.5s by feel to build although the wire's t14 reads 1250ms) plus two 20-damage taps drops a 115 pool in about 1s from release -- 3 trigger actions, 12 of the 40 rounds up, 84 of the roughly-103 heat budget (S43). The charge time is setup, not combat time: that is the weapon's identity. Forty up, eighty back -- three combo kills a magazine, ten across the kit.

weapons.name: Glock-18
weapons.desc: A machine pistol wearing a sidearm's badge. Empties in a blink and asks no questions.

based_on.why: no Callsign sidearm was ever captured; the Bolt Rifle frame is the one captured semi-automatic (t20=7, one shot per pull, no bolt pair, magazine reload) so it inherits the right trigger behaviour and $SIR row. Every deviation is a named wire/override token below.

t27.why: Glock-18 fire sound: ear 2026-09-11, P16 ("Deagle sound") preferred for the Glock over the earlier P09 ("a pronounced shot, could be the Deagle"); P09 is now unused. P16 is used by no other weapon, so a custom .LTP swapped in over the data port replaces only this pistol's shot

weapons.notes: The middle ground. 13 a hit at a measured cadence, 9 hits to drop, 16 in the mag with 64 behind it: 8 kills across the kit. Not the fastest trigger and not the biggest punch, but the safest bet not to be caught reloading.

weapons.name: USP-S
weapons.desc: A steady sidearm. It will not win a fight you started badly, but it will finish one you nearly had.
weapons.range_target_m: not set yet: sidearms keep the captured reach until the curve is mapped (S49)

t27.why: USP-S fire sound: sound-catalog id Q04, chosen from the on-gun gunshot families by descriptor (docs/reference/sound-catalog.md); Q04 is used by no other weapon, so a custom .LTP swapped in over the data port replaces only this pistol's shot

t26.why: USP-S is suppressed: half loudness, as on the captured Suppressor frame (t26=50)

weapons.notes: The quiet one. Suppressed and flashless: 9 a hit, as fast as you can pull the trigger, 13 hits to drop, 19 in the mag with 120 behind it: 10 kills across the kit. Low damage, but nobody hears where it came from. 2026-09-17: mag 20→19 -- Tony's ask was 20→14, but 14 leaves the Deagle strictly dominating the USP (its sustained DPS and one-magazine kill chance both fall too far once the mag is that shallow); 19 is the smallest cut off 20 that actually leaves neither pistol beating the other on every axis (a thin margin: sustained DPS differs by about 0.1 dmg/s, kill chance by 2 points).

weapons.name: Desert Eagle
weapons.desc: Rounds that hit like a rifle, and not many of them. Miss twice and you are reloading in front of someone.
weapons.range_target_m: not set yet: sidearms keep the captured reach until the curve is mapped (S49)

weapons.notes: The hand cannon. 26 a hit, five hits to drop — the most damage of any sidearm, if you land them. Seven in the mag, 48 behind it: 11 kills across the kit. A slow cycle that punishes every miss.

weapons.name: Rocket Launcher
weapons.desc: One round, one player, no argument. Two in the tube and nothing to reload from.
weapons.range_target_m: 8-10 indoor / 15-18 outdoor (Tony 2026-09-17: a one-shot kill is earned close, and these are pickup-only)
weapons.notes: Point, pull, erase. 115 a hit (a full-health operator in one) on the fastest power-tier cycle, with the slowest reload behind it. Four rounds, four kills, no second chances.

weapons.name: Rail Gun
weapons.desc: A single charged slug that ends whoever it finds. Two shots, and then it is scrap.
weapons.range_target_m: 8-10 indoor / 15-18 outdoor (Tony 2026-09-17: a one-shot kill is earned close, and these are pickup-only)
weapons.notes: Charges and fires itself. A 1.2s wind-up that goes whether you are ready or not, 115 on impact, four rounds total. Everyone within earshot hears the spool.

weapons.name: Laser Cannon
weapons.desc: A beam that does not ask about armour. Two shots and it is spent.
weapons.notes: Must be held to charge; a tap fires nothing at all. 1.5s of commitment for a guaranteed kill, and the fastest reload in the power tier for the trouble.

weapons.name: Energy Launcher
weapons.desc: Lobbed plasma. Whatever it lands near stops being your problem.

t27.why: ear 2026-09-11 (W4a audition, six O-family clips solo): O06 ("shooting a rocket") chosen over the earlier placeholder O01; O04 ("shooting a missile") was runner-up, O01/O02/O05 read as the BLAST not the launch, and O03 is a rifle shot. Original placeholder rationale: captured J15 is a music sting (J = music/SFX family, DK legend), inherited from the 'unnamed secondary' frame (bench 2026-08-26); the O family is otherwise unused by the stock arsenal

weapons.caution: Known issue: deals no damage in our shipped config (weapon-design.md). Avoid until fixed.
weapons.notes: No charge, no tell, no warning. 115 a hit with the fastest reload on the board and the slowest cycle in its tier. Four kills, spent quietly.

weapons.name: Ion Sniper
weapons.desc: One shot, any distance, nobody left standing. There are two of them and then there are none.
weapons.notes: A one-shot kill in a rifle's body. 115 a hit on a 1.4s cycle with two up and two back. The power tier's only weapon that looks and sounds like a marksman rifle.

weapons.name: Melee
weapons.desc: Everyone carries it and nobody chooses it. For the range where nothing else helps.
weapons.notes: Last resort: no ammo, no reload, a gyro swing with the butt of the gun. 90 on contact. Hidden from the picker, always bound to slot 4.

weapons.name: Breacher
weapons.range_target_m: 12 indoor / 25-30 outdoor (the SMG band: a support weapon has to be used from cover, not across the field)
weapons.desc: It cannot kill. It takes every layer of armour and shield off whoever you hit, and leaves the finishing to someone else.

based_on.why: no support weapon was ever captured. The Suppressor frame is the quiet, deep-magazine automatic, which is the right trigger feel for a tool you hold on a target rather than a gun you duel with. Every deviation is a named wire token below.

t3.why: keys the fn-20 support cell $SIR <5,0> (weapon-design.md §7.5/§7.6, bench 2026-09-18). The captured frame's own proto token stays 0, a verbatim copy of the Suppressor it is based on -- this is the sanctioned per-token deviation, not a re-capture.

weapons.notes: Strips armour and shields and cannot take a single point of health. Nine a hit off whatever they are wearing, through every layer in order, and the overflow carries: a full shield and a full plate come off in one magazine. Point it at a teammate instead and it REPAIRS them, because the same function that strips an enemy grants armour to an ally. You give up your backup gun to carry it, and you need someone else to finish what you start. Bench 2026-09-18: shield 120 to 0 then armour 70 to 0, health fixed at 999 the whole way, and eleven further hits on a bare target moved nothing at all.

weapons.name: Haze
weapons.range_target_m: 12 indoor / 25-30 outdoor (the SMG band: a support weapon has to be used from cover, not across the field)
weapons.desc: It cannot kill either. What it takes is a player's aim, for a few seconds, which is often worse.

based_on.why: no support weapon was ever captured. The Suppressor frame is the quiet, deep-magazine automatic, which is the right trigger feel for a tool you hold on a target rather than a gun you duel with. Every deviation is a named wire token below.

t3.why: keys the fn-23 support cell $SIR <7,0> (weapon-design.md §7.5/§7.6, bench 2026-09-18). The captured frame's own proto token stays 0, a verbatim copy of the Suppressor it is based on -- this is the sanctioned per-token deviation, not a re-capture.

weapons.caution: The Haze needs the HUD that tells a flashed player why nothing is landing (S53) before players meet it.
weapons.notes: A three-second blackout. The target keeps firing and keeps spending rounds, and every shot misses: their own gun goes quiet and the person they are aiming at hears the shots whizz past. It takes no health at all, and it wears off on its own. Use it to break a firing line, cross open ground, or take a point off someone who cannot afford three seconds. Bench 2026-09-18: live accuracy 100 to 0 in the same millisecond as the hit, recovering 0, 2, 4, 7, 12 over about three seconds, with nothing left behind.

weapons.name: Toxin Rifle
weapons.range_target_m: 18-20 indoor / 40-45 outdoor (the assault band: it has to hold a target, not snipe one)
weapons.desc: Hits lightly and keeps hitting. The damage arrives after you have stopped shooting, which is the whole point.
weapons.caution: NOT FINISHED. The gun applies the direct damage today; the poison is a tick clock on the player's own phone (S16, spec/node.md §3.17) and that is not built, so this row is hidden. Enabled early it is simply a worse SMG.

based_on.why: no poison weapon was ever captured. The SMG frame is the fast, shallow-magazine automatic, which is the right feel for a weapon that has to land several hits on one target rather than trade single shots. Every deviation is a named wire token below.

t3.why: keys the poison cell $SIR <11,0> (weapon-design.md, S16). The captured frame's own proto token stays 0, a verbatim copy of the SMG it is based on -- this is the sanctioned per-token deviation, not a re-capture.

weapons.notes: Every hit poisons. The rounds themselves are weak and the poison is the payload: bring somebody down to about twenty and break contact, and they die anyway. Fired straight it kills in 1.54 s against the standard pool, slower than an assault rifle, but you only need twelve hits to make the poison lethal, which is the same 1.21 s the rifle takes to finish the job outright. The difference is that you never see it land, and they might reach a station first. It is the one weapon that punishes an enemy for walking away.
